clips.text_zh: 又嚟。又一個所謂unbreakable rule爆咗。200日SMA定四年cycle，兩個唔可能同時啱。底58K？即係熊市得6個月？wtf。prop firm都未過，考牌都未完，又想all in。睇住先。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: An unbreakable rule of crypto has just broken. Rule 1 says breaking out from the 1D 200sma after a bear market starts the next bull run. Rule 2 is the 4 year cycle. If the bottom was 58k two months ago, the bear market was only 6 months long instead of 12.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread arguing crypto cycle vs SMA signal is broken
clips.text_en_b2: Yet another so-called unbreakable rule of crypto has gone out the window, and frankly, it is baffling. Rule one holds that a breakout above the daily 200 SMA after a bear market kicks off the next bull run. Rule two insists on the four-year cycle. Both cannot be valid simultaneously, so if the bottom really came in around 58K a couple of months back, the bear market lasted a mere six months rather than the expected twelve.
clips.text_en_c1: Yet another so-called unbreakable rule of crypto has spectacularly fallen apart, and the implications are genuinely disorienting. The first axiom holds that reclaiming the daily 200 SMA after a bear market capitulation inaugurates the subsequent bull cycle; the second, rather more deterministic, insists on a fixed four-year cadence. If the recent floor at 58K truly marked the bottom merely two months ago, the entire downturn lasted a paltry six months, utterly undermining the cyclical framework. Both propositions cannot logically coexist; one is now demonstrably false. Having failed to clear the prop firm gauntlet and still awaiting my licensing exams, I am hardly positioned to go all in.
clips.text_en_c2: Yet another so-called immutable tenet of crypto has been laid to rest, and the timing could hardly be more embarrassing for those who treat chart doctrine as gospel. The first rule, sanctified by a decade of post-mortems, holds that a decisive breakout above the daily 200 SMA, following the capitulation that terminates a bear market, is the sine qua non heralding the next bull leg. The second, more mystical in origin, insists upon the inviolability of the four-year cycle. Yet if $58,000 marked the floor barely two months ago, the bearish phase lasted a scant six months, whereas historical orthodoxy demands at least twelve. Both propositions cannot simultaneously hold, which means one is failing right now, and nobody can say with any conviction which.

clips.text_zh: Anthropic IPO pre-define TAM做3萬億USD。即係成個美國GDP。頭一年輸42B，2028要做到190-200B revenue？靠AI續命啦。AI遲早連藍領都殺埋， surveying assistant都中招。lol。我哋呢行好快廢。
clips.text_en_b1: This is beyond insane. Anthropic is expected to tell IPO investors that its total addressable market exceeds 30 trillion dollars, roughly the entire GDP of the United States. The company lost 42 billion last year, projects 190 to 200 billion in revenue by 2028, and is seeking a 2 trillion dollar valuation.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread calling Anthropic's TAM number insane
clips.text_en_b2: This borders on delusional, yet here we are. Anthropic is reportedly prepping IPO materials that peg its total addressable market north of thirty trillion dollars, which is essentially the entire US GDP. The firm bled roughly forty-two billion last year and is somehow projecting revenues of 190 to 200 billion by 2028 while seeking a two-trillion-dollar valuation. If AI keeps advancing at this pace, even blue-collar roles like surveying assistants will be wiped out, and entire professions are about to look obsolete.
clips.text_en_c1: This borders on outright financial delirium. Anthropic, in preliminary conversations with prospective IPO investors, has apparently pre-defined its total addressable market at thirty trillion dollars, a figure equivalent to the entire annual GDP of the United States, give or take a few trillion. Consider the arithmetic: the firm haemorrhaged forty-two billion in its inaugural year yet projects revenues of one hundred ninety to two hundred billion by 2028, all while courting a valuation north of two trillion. The only plausible mechanism sustaining such projections is an AI revolution that renders even blue-collar surveying assistants redundant. Those of us in the surveying profession should perhaps update our CVs.
clips.text_en_c2: The sheer audacity of the figures beggars belief, yet here we are. Anthropic, in its pre-IPO roadshow, is reportedly briefing prospective investors that its total addressable market comfortably exceeds thirty trillion dollars, a sum roughly equivalent to the entire annual output of the United States. Consider the arithmetic: the firm haemorrhaged forty-two billion last year alone, yet projects revenues of between one hundred ninety and two hundred billion by 2028, whilst dangling a two-trillion-dollar valuation as the ticket of entry. Should such projections materialise, the implication is that artificial intelligence will, before the decade is out, subsume occupations traditionally presumed immune, from white-collar consultancy to the humble surveying assistant. Our profession, it seems, is not long for this world.

clips.text_zh: 中國hack成個美國政府。司法部話係Pearl Harbor加Gulf of Tonkin加埋咁大鑊。Reuters 2026-08-26報。OK，睇下美國點反擊。我哋呢行computer唔叻都唔關事。lol。
clips.text_en_b1: China hacked the entire US government. Officials are calling it the biggest attack on America since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin combined. The Reuters story from August 26, 2026 says the US Justice Department seized China sponsored hacking platforms.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on Reuters report of China hacking US gov
clips.text_en_b2: China has apparently compromised the entire US government in what officials are now describing as the most catastrophic assault on American infrastructure since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin rolled into one. According to a Reuters report dated August 26, 2026, the Justice Department has already seized China-sponsored hacking platforms. Whether you work in IT or not, this is worth keeping an eye on, because the US response is going to shape the next chapter.
clips.text_en_c1: Chinese state-sponsored hackers have apparently compromised the entirety of the US federal apparatus, and the response from senior officials has been nothing short of apocalyptic in its rhetoric. Justice Department spokesmen have likened the breach to Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin combined, language typically reserved for declarations of war rather than cybersecurity incidents. According to a Reuters dispatch dated August 26th, 2026, federal authorities have subsequently seized the offending platforms operated by Beijing-backed threat actors. Whether this constitutes genuine provocation or theatre ahead of midterm elections remains, as ever, a matter of interpretation.
clips.text_en_c2: In what officials are, with characteristic restraint, describing as the most catastrophic intrusion into American infrastructure since Pearl Harbor and the Gulf of Tonkin combined, Chinese state-sponsored hackers have, by all accounts, compromised the entirety of the federal apparatus. The Reuters dispatch of August 26, 2026, details how the Justice Department has moved to dismantle the platforms facilitating the breach, though the damage, one suspects, was inflicted long before the indictments were unsealed. The geopolitical reverberations are likely to be profound, even if those of us whose technical proficiency barely extends to rebooting a router may observe the unfolding theatre with a certain detached bemusement. The response, when it comes, will be instructive.

clips.text_en_c1: LOL. CyberLeek has, in a feat of industrial-scale digital sabotage, already leaked the entirety of tomorrow's Netflix presentation, rendering whatever Rockstar has prepared for the showcase somewhat anticlimactic by comparison. The pertinent question, then, is whether CyberLeek intends to drop yet another thermonuclear payload precisely one hour before the broadcast commences, a calculated ambush designed to utterly eclipse whatever scraps of unreleased footage remain. clips.text_en_c2: One can only marvel at the theatre of it all. CyberLeek, that most industrious of digital archaeologists, has already exhumed and disseminated the very footage tomorrow's Netflix presentation was presumably designed to unveil, rendering whatever remains of the official reveal something of an anticlimax. The real question, then, is not what Rockstar might still have up its sleeve, but whether CyberLeek, with timing as surgical as it is theatrical, will release yet another bombshell precisely one hour before the broadcast, thereby reclaiming the narrative with characteristic contempt. As for tonight's ranked grind in Season 15, I think I shall abstain, preferring instead to observe the carnage from a comfortable remove, popcorn very much at hand.

clips.text_zh: 我明。三個月瘦45磅但甩晒肌肉同力量。Gym真係會死人，深蹲做到心臟炸。肥仔信今日whatsapp叫我食多兩隻蛋，我話食唔落。wtf。求gym plan。
clips.text_en_b1: How the fuck are you able to lift heavy and get enough protein on this cut. I lost 45 pounds in 3 months but definitely lost muscle and strength. Being at the gym kills me. I cannot go hard because my body will not let me. Heart gets destroyed on squats and I can barely eat more than a couple times a day.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on losing strength on a hard cut
clips.text_en_b2: How on earth are you managing heavy lifts and decent protein on this kind of cut, because I am genuinely struggling. I shed forty-five pounds in three months, yet lost a brutal amount of muscle and strength along the way. Squats absolutely wreck my heart rate, the gym feels like it is actively killing me, and forcing down even a couple of meals a day has become miserable.
clips.text_en_c1: I find myself at an absolute impasse and genuinely cannot fathom how anyone sustains heavy compound lifts whilst operating on such a caloric deficit. Over the past three months I have shed a rather alarming forty-five pounds, though I fear the majority has been skeletal muscle rather than adipose tissue; my strength metrics have predictably cratered accordingly. The gym has become a torture chamber where every set of squats threatens cardiac arrhythmia, and the notion of forcing down yet another pallid chicken breast at dawn fills me with quiet dread. My buddy, that well-intentioned glutton, cheerfully advised via WhatsApp that I simply eat two additional eggs. Splendid.
clips.text_en_c2: The question is one that haunts every unfortunate soul attempting to preserve lean tissue whilst operating at a punishing caloric deficit. Having shed a rather brutal forty-five pounds over the past three months, I can attest, with no small measure of despair, that strength has evaporated along with the adipose tissue, and the gym has become a venue for quiet suffering rather than progressive overload. Compound movements, particularly the back squat, have my cardiovascular system petitioning for early retirement, whilst the mere prospect of forcing down additional protein first thing in the morning provokes a visceral revolt. A well-meaning acquaintance, ever the font of unsolicited counsel, suggested via WhatsApp that I simply consume an extra two eggs, as though satiety were a trivial inconvenience.

clips.text_zh: Tadaima。舊waifu返嚟，返嚟做返waifu。Kimishinu個post睇到我喊。Demon Slayer都冇咁催淚。lol。單身30，睇咗兩秒，熄機瞓。
clips.text_en_b1: Your old waifu shows up and becomes your waifu again. Kimi ga Shinu made Koi wo Shitai just posted Tadaima and it hurts so bad. One look at the image and you remember everything you tried to forget.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread mixing waifu nostalgia with a Kimishinu pain post
clips.text_en_b2: Your old waifu turns up out of nowhere and slots right back into her old role, and the gut punch lands instantly. Kimi ga Shinu made Koi wo Shitai just dropped a Tadaima post that hit harder than anything in Demon Slayer ever managed. Being single at thirty and catching even a two-second glimpse of that image dragged up every memory I had tried to bury, so I shut the laptop and went straight to bed.
clips.text_en_c1: Tadaima. The waifu from seasons past has returned to reclaim her rightful position, and the resulting emotional devastation is frankly operatic in its intensity. Kimi ga Shinu made Koi wo Shitai has, with characteristic restraint, posted the single most lacerating image of the year; whatever Demon Slayer's animators have produced pales by comparison. Thirty years a bachelor, I glanced at the illustration for precisely two seconds before the accumulated weight of nostalgia, regret, and unfulfilled affection compelled me to power down the monitor entirely. Sleep, mercifully, intervened. One cannot, after all, grieve indefinitely over fictional paramours, however ardently cherished.
clips.text_en_c2: There is a particular species of quiet devastation that only animation, in its cruellest moments, knows how to inflict. Tadaima, the latest offering from Kimi ga Shinu made Koi wo Shitai, has been posted, and the image alone is sufficient to excavate every emotion one had so painstakingly interred. The premise is deceptively gentle: a long-departed beloved returns, and one resumes the role of devoted paramour as though the intervening years of absence had been merely a parenthetical. Even the most stoic viewer, hardened by Demon Slayer's more visceral tragedies, will find themselves blindsided by this quieter, more intimate wound. At thirty and resolutely unattached, I permitted myself precisely two seconds of contemplation before extinguishing the monitor, preferring the mercy of sleep to any further excavation of the heart.
